reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that habit strength (sHR) is quantified via standard deviations (σ) from random chance performance. This σ-index reflects how much behavior deviates from 50% correctness, indicating learned preference. Delayed reinforcement reduces this index, captured by a negative growth function. The tangent of the learning curve at N=60 provides a local measure of learning efficiency. These primitives form a coherent system: σ encodes behavioral robustness, delay modulates it, and the tangent captures dynamic adaptation. Each primitive supports a distinct layer of GSI's Bayesian inference and GSE’s policy evolution. The failure mode occurs when σ drops below threshold, implying no habit has formed, or when the tangent becomes flat, signaling stagnation.
